属性断言：The zeros correspond to the signal transmission-blocking properties of the system and are also called the transmission zeros. The system has the inherent capability to block frequencies coinciding with its zero locations.
属性断言：Moving a zero closer to a specific pole reduces the relative contribution of that mode to the output response; zeros directly impact the constants A_i and D_k in Equation (5.22).
属性断言：Derivative interpretation of zero effect on step response
属性断言：For a second-order system with a zero, the major effect of the zero is to increase the overshoot M_p and reduce rise time t_r, while having very little influence on settling time.
属性断言：If there is a zero near the pole at s = -σ_i, then A_i will be much smaller in magnitude.
属性断言：Complex zeros near lightly damped poles reduce oscillations
属性断言：A zero in the RHP will depress the overshoot (and may cause the step response to start out in the wrong direction).
属性断言：Moving a zero closer to a specific pole will reduce the relative contribution to the output response.
例 3.1 中的系统具有传递函数 H(s)=1/(s+k)。
属性断言：若闭环零、极点彼此接近，则它们对系统响应速度的影响会相互削弱。
属性断言：闭环零点对系统阻尼的影响
属性断言：Figure 5.13 shows the time-domain response y(t) of a second-order transfer function with a zero for four values of the ratio a/ζω_n = 0.5, 1, 2, and 10.0 when ζ=0.45.
属性断言：If a ≫ ζω_n and τ ≪ 1/ζω_n, then the pole and zero will have minimal effect on the step response.
属性断言：Zero near pole reduces coefficient of that mode in partial-fraction expansion
属性断言：Zeros correspond to signal transmission-blocking properties
属性断言：闭环零点对系统时间响应形状的影响
属性断言：The poles of T(s) determine the particular response modes that will be present, and the zeros of T(s) establish the relative weightings of the individual mode functions.
属性断言：闭环零点会减小峰值时间，使系统响应速度加快，超调量增大，即减小系统阻尼，且这种作用将随闭环零点接近虚轴而加剧。

属性断言：If the transfer function of a system possesses a finite zero and it is located relatively near the dominant complex poles, then the zero will materially affect the transient response of the system.
属性断言：Effect of zero on overshoot and rise time for second-order system
属性断言：When the zero is in the right half-plane (RHP), the derivative term is subtracted rather than added, causing an initial response in the 'wrong direction' (nonminimum-phase behavior).

属性断言：For H(s) = (24/z)*(s+z)/((s+4)(s+6)), the step response is y(t) = 1 + (12/z - 3)e^{-4t} + (2 - 12/z)e^{-6t}. When z=4 or z=6, one mode vanishes (pole-zero cancellation). The zero closest to the origin (z=1) produces the largest overshoot.
属性断言：The only significant effect of the nonminimum-phase zero was to cause the initial response to go in the 'wrong direction' and make the response somewhat sluggish.
属性断言：Nonminimum-phase zero causes initial response in wrong direction
属性断言：As the ratio a/ζω_n increases, the finite zero moves farther into the left half-plane and away from the poles, and the step response approaches the second-order system response.

属性断言：For H(s) = ((s+α)^2+β^2)/((s+1)[(s+0.1)^2+1]), when complex zeros exactly cancel the lightly damped poles (α=0.1, β=1.0), oscillations are eliminated. When zeros are not close, oscillations appear in the step response.
属性断言：Zeros near poles reduce the coefficient of the corresponding exponential term in the partial-fraction expansion, thereby diminishing that term's contribution to the total response.

属性断言：The transfer function h(s)/δ_e(s) = 30(s-6)/(s(s^2+4s+13)). The RHP zero at s=6 causes an initial drop in altitude (nonminimum-phase behavior). The final value is h(∞)=13.8 ft. Estimated rise time t_r=0.5 sec, overshoot M_p=0.14, settling time t_s=2.3 sec; actual values from Matlab are t_r≈0.43 sec, M_p≈0.14, t_s≈2.6 sec.
属性断言：A zero in the left half-plane (LHP) will increase the overshoot if the zero is within a factor of 4 of the real part of the complex poles.
属性断言：The roots of the numerator are called the finite zeros of the system. Zeros are locations in the s-plane where the transfer function is zero.
属性断言：Effect of zero between two poles on overshoot
属性断言：After control design, the time response should always be checked by exact calculation, usually by numerical simulation, to verify whether time specifications have been met.
